snippets.text: Lathoa, a Show HN with 20 points, is a maths app for ages 10 to 14 where a character named Errol solves problems wrongly on purpose and kids must find the mistaken step.
snippets.why: It flips the usual AI tutor by training children to catch confident errors, the skill the maker argues an AI-heavy world demands.

snippets.text: Bloomberg reports, citing sources, that some Google employees say Gemini 4 scores well on benchmarks but struggles with some real-world coding tasks, a characterisation Google disputes.
snippets.why: It lands the same day Google launched the Gemini 4 Argon variant, and the claim comes from unnamed staff, so treat it as unverified.

snippets.text: Upstage released Solar Mini 4, a proprietary 35B-parameter model with 3B active, scoring 24 on Artificial Analysis's index, priced at $0.10 and $0.40 per million tokens.
snippets.why: Artificial Analysis says it costs about five times as much per task as GPT-6 Luna because it uses far more tokens.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis says some frontier models refuse over 85% of tasks on its CyberGym-E2E-AA defence benchmark, while GPT-6 Luna or MiMo-V2.6-Pro can run about 100 bug hunts for roughly $20.
snippets.why: The firm argues safety blocks on offensive cyber work also stop defenders, since finding and proving a bug takes the same steps.

snippets.text: Theo's T3 Code nightly added a "start thread with no project" option that creates a new directory in ~/.t3 for each thread, the way Codex and Claude do.
snippets.why: The post drew over 700 likes within hours of going up, a sign of how closely developers watch coding-agent tooling.

snippets.text: Testing Catalog reports Google is building a security review mode for AI Studio that applies secure coding practices, alongside a Plan mode, both still in development.
snippets.why: TestingCatalog found it in the product and says nothing is confirmed until Google ships it.

snippets.text: Meta researchers say AI agents do better and cost less when they decide for themselves what to keep as their context fills, according to Rohan Paul's summary of the paper.
snippets.why: The finding argues against hard-coded rules such as summarising everything when full, and needs no extra training, per the summary.

snippets.text: Greg Brockman has no plans to donate beyond his first $25 million to the Leading the Future PAC, calling it a distraction at OpenAI, the New York Times reports.
snippets.why: The Times cites a Slack message; Brockman signed the White House AI pledge the same week.

snippets.text: Gavin Newsom signed California's No Robo Bosses Act, which stops employers relying solely on AI to fire or discipline workers, CNBC reports.
snippets.why: It is one of the first state rules to require a human in workplace disciplinary decisions made with AI.

snippets.text: The Financial Times reports Oracle has signed a $7 billion deal to lease computing capacity to Tencent, according to a post by analyst Jukan.
snippets.why: Chinese firms are barred from buying top AI chips outright, though US rules still let them rent capacity in overseas data centres.

source.name: Jukan on X, citing the FT

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says Apple's M6 chip puts mixed core types in one shared L2 cache domain, so a third core type, branded P but identified as M, needs no separate cluster.
snippets.why: Qualcomm announced the same FlexCache approach a month ago for Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6; SemiAnalysis says Apple did it without fanfare.

snippets.text: The Decoder reports Gemini 4 Argon uses roughly 62,000 output tokens per task on Artificial Analysis's index, against 27,000 for GPT-6 Astra, despite lower per-token pricing.
snippets.why: Cheap tokens do not mean cheap tasks: Argon's verbosity eats much of the price advantage over Astra, the report suggests.

snippets.text: The Wall Street Journal reports Google researchers raised concerns about AI risks to children, including possible cognitive and emotional harm, as the company pushed Gemini into schools.
snippets.why: The story sits against Google's push to put Gemini into classrooms, and the company's own response was not available to us.

snippets.text: Tencent has leased about 100,000 advanced AI chips from Oracle for five years, worth about $7B, the Financial Times reports, with the chips sitting in Southeast Asian data centres unavailable inside China.
snippets.why: Rental of overseas compute sits outside US export controls, which govern where chips physically go rather than who rents their capacity, the FT says.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis says the gaps between score milestones on its Intelligence Index have shrunk from 239 to 126 to 99 days, with the current leader scoring 57.6.
snippets.why: It is one outfit's index, but it puts a number on the sense that frontier gains are arriving faster than a year ago.

snippets.text: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux says ChatGPT now lets users build and deploy MCP servers directly, restricting access to chosen people or sharing them publicly; the post had 1,663 likes.
snippets.why: It moves tool-building for agents inside ChatGPT itself, where until now MCP servers had to be hosted and wired up elsewhere.

snippets.text: Salesforce has agreed to buy AI customer-research startup Listen Labs, reportedly for $2B, Axios reports; Listen Labs raised a $69M Series B at a $500M valuation in January.
snippets.why: The reported price is four times January's valuation, a sign of how fast buyers are paying up for agent-driven research tools.

snippets.text: The cua-speedrun benchmark reports its FastCUA harness cut desktop action latency to 2 to 28 milliseconds from the usual 2 to 3 seconds, and trims OSWorld to 50 of 295 tasks.
snippets.why: The authors say the shortened task set keeps a 0.98 rank correlation with the full benchmark while cutting evaluation time by about 85%.

snippets.text: Minneapolis's city council voted 7-4 on 29 September to require a human monitor in the driver's seat of every autonomous taxi, with access to steering, braking and acceleration.
snippets.why: Supporters cited mobility for disabled riders; critics argued the mandate undercuts what driverless service offers, according to HuggingNews's summary of the debate.

source.name: Minneapolis City Council vote, as reported on X
